# ui-sdk for Ember

> ember-ui-sdk renders ui-sdk's framework-free TypeScript core in Ember. How an interface behaves lives in the core; ember-ui-sdk turns each primitive into parts. No styles, no dependencies, no providers, no portals.

This file is the context an agent needs to build with ember-ui-sdk: how Ember renders a primitive and the conventions every part shares, then every component with a link to its page. Read the pages of the components you use. It's generated from the docs, for this release.

- [Core](./core.md): build a component, compose behaviors, and explore the foundations, from defining a primitive to working with state, the browser and text.
- [Agents](./agents.md): letting an agent operate a page, and WebMCP.

## Introduction

These docs cover ui-sdk in Ember. Using another framework? See React, Vue, Svelte, Solid or Web Components. To build your own components from behaviors, see [Core](./core.md).

`ember-ui-sdk` gives you Glimmer components such as Tabs, Popover, and Select, built on ui-sdk's behaviors. They handle interactions, focus, and ARIA attributes. You choose their markup and styles.

Import a component's root, use the parts it yields, and style them with your own CSS.

### Quick Start

Copy this prompt into your agent:

```text prompt
Set up ui-sdk in this Ember project. It needs Ember 7 or newer, with template tag (.gts) components.

1. Install ember-ui-sdk and @ui-sdk/core with the project's package manager.
2. Add a note to AGENTS.md, creating it if needed: before using ui-sdk, follow the ui-sdk skill if it's installed, and read node_modules/ember-ui-sdk/docs/llms.txt. To build a new component, also search node_modules/ember-ui-sdk/docs/core.md by heading, and read rendering.md next to it.
3. If you support skills, run: npx skills add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk
```

It installs ui-sdk and points your `AGENTS.md` at the docs that ship with the packages.

### Set It Up Yourself

- [Installation](./installation.md): Install the packages in your Ember app.
- [Components](./README.md): Browse the components with live examples.

## Installation

Start with an app using Ember 7 or newer, with template tag components in `.gts` files.

### Install the Packages

```bash
npm install ember-ui-sdk @ui-sdk/core
```

`ember-ui-sdk` provides the Glimmer components. `@ui-sdk/core` provides their behavior and is a peer dependency. Install both so the components and any helpers you use share one copy of the core.

### Use a Component

Import each component's root from its own entry. The root yields its parts, so a template needs only the one import:

```gts
import { Tabs } from "ember-ui-sdk/tabs"

<template>
  <Tabs @defaultValue="account" as |t|>
    <t.List aria-label="Settings">
      <t.Tab @value="account">Account</t.Tab>
      <t.Tab @value="password">Password</t.Tab>
    </t.List>
    <t.Panel @value="account">Manage your profile.</t.Panel>
    <t.Panel @value="password">Choose a new password.</t.Panel>
  </Tabs>
</template>
```

Options are arguments, like `@defaultValue`, and callbacks are arguments too, like `@onValueChange`. HTML attributes, like `aria-label`, go to the part's element. Each entry also exports every part by name, like `TabsList`, for templates that import them directly.

Each [component page](./README.md) lists the parts a root yields.

### Add Your Styles

Components are unstyled, so you style them with your app's CSS or with Tailwind CSS. Every part sets a `data-slot`, such as `tabs-tab`, and its state as data attributes, such as `data-selected`.

For a default look to start from, import `@ui-sdk/core/web.css` once, at the top of your app's entry:

```ts
import "@ui-sdk/core/web.css"
```

With Tailwind CSS, import it in your global stylesheet instead, after Tailwind. `layer(components)` puts it above Tailwind's base styles, so they don't reset it, and below its utilities, so a class still wins:

```css
@layer ui-sdk;

@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@ui-sdk/core/web.css" layer(components);
```

You can render your first component without setting up a provider or adding a portal root.

### Right to Left

Set `dir="rtl"` on the page or a container. Arrow keys and popup placement follow that direction without a provider. Use logical CSS properties, such as `padding-inline-start`, for your styles.

## Utilities

### Async Options

`useAsyncOptions` loads items as someone types. It waits for typing to pause, cancels requests that are replaced, and keeps the previous results visible while loading.

Change the movie search and wait for the results. Use the arrow keys to choose a movie, then press Enter.

#### Load Results

Call the helper in a component class, passing the component as its owner and a loader. This example expects `/api/movies` to return an array of movie titles:

```gts
import Component from "@glimmer/component"
import { useAsyncOptions } from "ember-ui-sdk/async-options"
import { Combobox } from "ember-ui-sdk/combobox"

export default class Movies extends Component {
  movies = useAsyncOptions(this, async (query, { signal }) => {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/movies?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, {
      signal,
    })
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Couldn't load movies")
    return response.json()
  })

  onQueryChange = (query: string) => {
    this.movies.setQuery(query)
  }

  <template>
    <Combobox
      @items={{this.movies.state.items}}
      @filter={{false}}
      @status={{this.movies.state.status}}
      @onQueryChange={{this.onQueryChange}}
      as |c|
    >
      <c.Label>Movie</c.Label>
      <c.Input placeholder="Search movies…" />
      <c.Content>
        <c.Status as |s|>{{s.state.status}}</c.Status>
        <c.Empty>No movies match.</c.Empty>
        <c.List as |list|>
          {{#each list.state.items key="@identity" as |movie|}}
            <c.Item @value={{movie}} @label={{movie}}>{{movie}}</c.Item>
          {{/each}}
        </c.List>
      </c.Content>
    </Combobox>
  </template>
}
```

Read `this.movies.state` in the template so Glimmer tracks it. Copying the state into a plain variable keeps only its value at that moment.

Pass `signal` to `fetch` so a newer search can cancel the request. The helper cancels on destroy. `@filter={{false}}` leaves matching and ordering to the server.

Use `c.Status` and `c.Empty` to show loading, error, and empty messages, as in the demo. The same pattern works with [Select](./components/select.md#async-search), [Autocomplete](./components/autocomplete.md#async-suggestions), and [Command](./components/command.md#async-results).

#### Choose When to Load

The third argument sets the starting behavior:

| Option      | What It Does                                            | Default |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `debounce`  | Milliseconds typing must pause before a request starts. | `200`   |
| `query`     | The starting search text.                               | `""`    |
| `immediate` | Loads that text as soon as the component mounts.        | `false` |

```ts
movies = useAsyncOptions(this, searchMovies, { immediate: true, debounce: 300 })
```

For initial choices, use `immediate: true`. Until that first load starts, `status` is already `"loading"`, so the list never flashes an empty state. If you set `query`, use the same starting text for the combobox's `@defaultQuery`.

#### Load More

For paged results, the loader receives `page`, starting at `0`. Return `{ items, hasMore }`:

```ts
import type { AsyncOptionsContext } from "ember-ui-sdk/async-options"

async function loadMoviePages(
  query: string,
  { signal, page }: AsyncOptionsContext
) {
  const response = await fetch(
    `/api/movies?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&page=${page}`,
    { signal }
  )
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Couldn't load movies")
  const data: { titles: string[]; next: number | null } = await response.json()
  return { items: data.titles, hasMore: data.next !== null }
}

export { loadMoviePages }
```

Pass `loadMoviePages` to `useAsyncOptions` in place of the inline loader above.

Pass `@onLoadMore` to Combobox, with a method that calls `this.movies.loadMore()`. Combobox asks for another page when scrolling or keyboard navigation reaches the last item. The helper appends the new items.

Open the movie list and scroll down, or use Arrow Down to reach the last result. The next page is added to the list.

#### Retry a Search

`status` is `"loading"` during a request, `"error"` after a failure, and `"idle"` otherwise. `error` holds the failure, and the previous items stay available.

Call `this.movies.reload()` from a retry button to load the current query again, starting at page `0`. `this.movies.state.hasMore` tells you whether another page is available.

### Custom Parts

The generated components are enough until one needs its own logic. You can write a root that creates a primitive's instance and a part that binds one slot of it, using the `rating.ts` definition from [Compose Behaviors](./core.md#complete-primitive).

#### Write a Root

`usePrimitive` creates the instance from the component's arguments for the life of the component. `usePart` binds the `root` slot, and `syncOptions` hands the arguments to the instance whenever they change. Put it first in the template:

```gts title="rating-root.gts"
import Component from "@glimmer/component"
import { syncOptions, usePart, usePrimitive } from "ember-ui-sdk/primitive"
import { rating } from "./rating"

export default class RatingRoot extends Component {
  handle = usePrimitive(this, rating)
  root = usePart(this, () => this.handle, "root")

  <template>
    {{syncOptions this.handle}}
    <div ...attributes {{this.root.modifier}}>{{yield}}</div>
  </template>
}
```

Controlled options follow data down and actions up: `@value` with `@onValueChange`. Pass a third argument to `usePrimitive` for options the arguments don't hold.

A child part takes the root's `handle` as an argument and calls `usePart` with its own slot. A part's `present`, `attrs`, `state` and `modifier` track what they read.

#### Type What a Root Yields

The roots type what they yield, so `c.part`, `c.state` and `c.Panel` check in strict templates, `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` included. Type your own root's block the same way: `RootYield` gives the `part` modifier, the slot's `state` and the `handle`, and `WithBoundArgs` each part with the arguments the root binds.

```gts title="rating-root.gts"
import Component from "@glimmer/component"
import { hash } from "@ember/helper"
import type { WithBoundArgs } from "@glint/template"
import {
  syncOptions,
  usePart,
  usePrimitive,
  type RootYield,
} from "ember-ui-sdk/primitive"
import { rating } from "./rating"
import RatingStar from "./rating-star"

export default class RatingRoot extends Component<{
  Blocks: {
    default: [
      RootYield<typeof rating> & {
        Star: WithBoundArgs<typeof RatingStar, "handle">
      },
    ]
  }
}> {
  handle = usePrimitive(this, rating)
  root = usePart(this, () => this.handle, "root")

  <template>
    {{syncOptions this.handle}}
    <div ...attributes {{this.root.modifier}}>{{yield
        (hash
          part=this.root.modifier
          state=this.root.state
          handle=this.handle
          Star=(component RatingStar handle=this.handle)
        )
      }}</div>
  </template>
}
```

A root bound to another slot, like a group's, names it: `RootYield<typeof radioGroup, "group">`. The `part` modifier binds any element, so it also fits a `ModifierLike<{ Element: HTMLElement }>`.

#### Bind a Part From Another Component

Ember has no context, so a part finds its root through an argument. A root that yields a part component of your own binds its instance to it with `(component)`, and the part hands that instance to `usePart`. The part binds to that root wherever it renders: in the root's template, or in the block of the app that uses the root.

```gts title="app-tabs.gts"
import Component from "@glimmer/component"
import { hash } from "@ember/helper"
import type { WithBoundArgs } from "@glint/template"
import { tabs, type TabsPrimitive } from "@ui-sdk/core/tabs"
import {
  syncOptions,
  usePart,
  usePrimitive,
  type PrimitiveHandle,
} from "ember-ui-sdk/primitive"

class AppTab extends Component<{
  Element: HTMLButtonElement
  Args: {
    /** The tabs' instance, which AppTabs binds. */
    handle?: PrimitiveHandle<TabsPrimitive>
    value: string
  }
  Blocks: { default: [] }
}> {
  part = usePart(
    this,
    () => this.args.handle,
    "tab",
    () => ({ value: this.args.value })
  )

  <template>
    <button type="button" ...attributes {{this.part.modifier}}>{{yield}}</button>
  </template>
}

export default class AppTabs extends Component<{
  Blocks: { default: [{ Tab: WithBoundArgs<typeof AppTab, "handle"> }] }
}> {
  handle = usePrimitive(this, tabs)
  list = usePart(this, () => this.handle, "list")

  <template>
    {{syncOptions this.handle}}
    <div {{this.list.modifier}}>
      {{yield (hash Tab=(component AppTab handle=this.handle))}}
    </div>
  </template>
}
```

```gts
<AppTabs as |t|>
  <t.Tab @value="a">Alpha</t.Tab>
  <t.Tab @value="b">Beta</t.Tab>
</AppTabs>
```

`WithBoundArgs` leaves `@handle` out of the type the app sees, so the instance stays between your root and your part. Keep it in an argument rather than a module-level map: the argument follows Ember's rendering, so each root's parts bind to that root, and nothing outlives it.

If `handle` returns nothing when the part is created, the part is detached for its life: it's present, its state is empty, and its modifier binds nothing. The same component then renders inside its root or alone, and TypeScript types its state as possibly missing.
